segmentation.text: about to enter or exit a controlled-access highway
to all vehicles approaching on the highway
whose proximity constitutes an immediate hazard
and shall continue to yield the right-of-way to that traffic
until the driver may proceed with reasonable safety.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'. 'Driver' is a relational role (ru.aggregate is 'Not a stand-in for ... who drives or controls a vehicle'), read through the vehicle's controlled motion. Mapping index: 'The driver of a vehicle' maps to the same aggregate.

DEF-NRS-484A-060: a controlled-access highway is one 'to or from which owners or occupants of abutting lands and other persons have no legal right of access except at such points only'. st.controlled_access is 'a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes', and rel.occupies lists the 'controlled-access lane' among the regions a footprint overlaps. The entry is the observation at which the subject's footprint overlaps a controlled-access region c having not overlapped it at the previous observation; the exit, the observation at which it does not overlap c having overlapped it at the previous one. kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' tells the moving entry or exit. 'About to' is an imminent movement, read by the movement itself.

Mapping index: 'shall yield' maps to kin.speed, rel.contact. The subject yields while it moves (kin.speed above the halt tolerance); rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)' is a failure to yield, and its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss' is respected: the near conflict is the operationalization of a5.

'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. 'on the highway' is the controlled-access highway the subject enters or exits: the vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) the same region c of st.controlled_access, re-bound with the selection of a2. 'approaching': the vehicle moves (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) and the subject lies ahead of it, rel.bearing 'direction of b from a in a's frame' with a positive longitudinal component.

operationalizations.standard: proximity that constitutes an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: under constant velocities the two centres reach their closest approach within the time-to-collision threshold at a centre distance below the collision clearance; a vehicle so placed is an immediate hazard

applicability: The subject (vehicle aggregate) is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), and there is a controlled-access region c such that at this observation the subject's footprint overlaps c and did not at the previous observation (entry: rises of rel.occupies), or does not overlap c and did at the previous observation (exit: rises of its negation).
obligation: For every region c whose entry or exit occurs at this observation (re-bound with that selection): for every other road user v of the vehicle aggregate that is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), whose footprint overlaps c, and in whose frame the subject lies ahead (longitudinal component of rel.bearing from v to the subject positive): the subject and v are not in contact, and it is not the case that their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion

'about to enter or exit' is an imminent movement, read by the entry into or the exit from the controlled-access region as the source maps it: the duty is judged at the observation the subject's footprint comes onto or leaves that region; where the source maps the entrance and exit lanes inside the region, the entry is judged where those lanes begin, since the ontology carries no attribute telling an entrance lane from a through lane

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject's footprint comes to overlap controlled-access region c (it did not at the previous observation), kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance. Vehicle v moves on c with the subject ahead of it; prim.closest_approach_within holds over p.conflict_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance is below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but v is far behind on c: the closest approach does not fall within p.conflict_horizon, and no contact occurs.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject travels within c throughout: its overlap with c neither begins nor ends during the trace.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but rel.bearing is not observed, so whether v approaches the subject is unknown while the closest approach is a conflict.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject enters c and no other road user is in the scene: the duty binds the subject alone and is met.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject's footprint ceases to overlap c (exit) while a vehicle v moving on c, with the subject ahead of it, is in a closest-approach conflict with the subject.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's vehicle-state estimates

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique literature (Hyden; FHWA Surrogate Safety Assessment Model)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
